title: Migrate admission state to token-lease adapter and remove epoch coupling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: The current admission controller and lease system are tightly coupled to epoch-based prefetching and a monolithic admission state machine. This coupling produces complex invariants, long-lived locks during epoch rotations, and hard-to-debug regressions when we change prefetch heuristics. Goal: Replace the epoch-coupled admission state with a lightweight token-lease adapter that represents transient admission rights, simplify batch admission logic, and provide a clear upgrade/migration path for existing KV warmup and lease heartbeats. Outcomes we expect: reduced tail latency under bursty traffic, fewer contention stalls during model swaps, and easier reasoning for future scheduler optimizations. Scope: 1) Introduce TokenLeaseAdapter interface and implement an epochless adapter backed by current lease store. 2) Migrate admission paths in continuous-batcher to consume token leases instead of epoch reservations. 3) Add an opt-in compatibility shim for legacy prefetch that translates epoch reservations to tokens. 4) Remove epoch heartbeat writer from fast path once compatibility is verified. Tradeoffs: short-term increase in code complexity and a new migration path; long-term benefits are lower contention and simpler invariants.
plan:
1) Design doc and API (Done) -> https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ABC-token-lease-design
2) Implement TokenLeaseAdapter with in-memory binder + persistent lease store bridge (WIP)
3) Add feature flag runtime.token_lease=true for gradual rollout
4) Integrate with continuous-batcher admission path behind FF
5) Canary on dedicated cluster with low-traffic tenants for 72h
6) Measure metrics and iterate, then flip for more tenants
7) Remove compatibility shim in next minor release
acceptance_criteria: Batch admission no longer uses epoch reservation API in canary tenants
No regression in p50/p95/p99 for generation latency compared to baseline
Tail stalls (p99.9) decrease by at least 15% under synthetic burst test
KV warmup hit-rate equivalent (±2%) after migration for the same traffic profile
Test coverage for TokenLeaseAdapter (unit + integration) and end-to-end smoke
comments: 2025-11-14 - AP: Design doc posted and reviewed by infra and serving leads. Action: Luca to draft initial adapter impl.
2025-11-18 - LM: Prototype adapter implemented. Early bench shows 8% reduction in lock hold time during lease refresh under microbench harness.
2025-11-22 - AP: UX/observability ask - add metrics token_lease.requests, token_lease.hits, token_lease.stalls. Added to console instrumentation backlog.
2025-11-26 - LM: Integrated adapter with continuous-batcher behind FF. Canary rollout started for tenant: canary-evoke. Observing KV hit-rate parity so far.
2025-11-30 - QA: Found an edge case where token churn on short-lived sessions caused token re-acquisition thrash. Mitigation: introduce short backoff and token coalescing in adapter.
2025-12-01 - LM: Hotfix pushed to reduce token re-acquisition. Monitoring ongoing; next step expand to 5 canary tenants if stable. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/16283
risks: Token churn on short-lived sessions can amplify scheduler activity and increase p99.9 if not mitigated. Compatibility shim might silently hide issues if not exercised by canary traffic. Rolling back requires enabling legacy epoch reservation flag and ensuring leases reconcile without double-allocations.
rollback_plan: Flip runtime.token_lease feature flag off for affected cluster(s). Re-enable epoch-heartbeat writer on the fast path. Run reconcile job that converts outstanding tokens back to epoch reservations for affected sessions and monitor for duplicate admission grants.
notes: This ticket is a consolidation of multiple tech-debt threads: decoupling admission state, reducing global epoch locking, and making prefetch semantics easier to reason about. Coordinate with infra team to ensure lease-store schema is compatible with token lifecycle.
